draft_text: Thornbill-NER appears somewhat robust to label noise in its training annotations.
revised_text: Under the pre-specified robustness criterion (mean test F1 drop ≤ 2.0 points), Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise at 10%, 20% and 30% noise rates, with mean F1 drops of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.8 points respectively.
rationale: T2.r1-r3 show Thornbill-NER drops of 0.6, 1.3, 1.8 points, all within the pre-specified 2.0-point robustness criterion at every noise rate. The evidence supports a stronger, criterion-based claim than the hedged "appears somewhat robust."

judgement.proposition: Thornbill-NER is somewhat robust to label noise in training annotations
judgement.strongest_supported: Under the pre-specified criterion (mean test F1 drop ≤ 2.0 points), Thornbill-NER is robust to label noise at 10%, 20% and 30% noise rates (drops of 0.6, 1.3 and 1.8 points), whereas Lindgren-Tagger is not (drops of 2.6, 5.5 and 8.9 points).
